claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 initially forms a high-temperature BCC solid solution.
The metastability of the initial BCC phase is controlled by the development of local chemical ordering.
Al segregates from the BCC solid solution during cooling or thermal exposure.
Al segregation produces nanoscale locally ordered clusters within the BCC matrix.
Local chemical ordering creates enhanced short-range order that reduces atomic mobility.
The reduced atomic mobility raises the nucleation barrier for equilibrium phases.
The reduced atomic mobility retards the growth of equilibrium phases.
Kinetic retardation caused by local ordering stabilizes the high-temperature BCC structure during cooling and initial thermal exposure.
Faster cooling will retain a higher fraction of disordered BCC than slower cooling or moderate annealing.
Rapidly cooled samples will contain minimal local-chemical-ordering features.
Slower cooling will increase the population of ordered clusters.
Moderate annealing will increase chemical segregation or ordered-phase formation.
Moderate annealing will increase the fraction of secondary phases associated with the ordering reaction.
Rapidly quenched baseline samples will be predominantly BCC with little nanoscale ordering or secondary-phase formation.
The proposed mechanism applies during moderate thermal exposures below approximately 700 degrees Celsius.
The proposed kinetic mechanism ceases to control phase stability after sufficiently long, high-temperature annealing produces equilibrium segregation.
Marked compositional deviations can alter local segregation behavior enough to invalidate the proposed mechanism.

contradictions.description: The mechanism says that ordered clusters stabilize BCC by impeding transformation, but the predicted outcome associates minimal ordering with the greatest BCC retention and increased ordering with a greater secondary-phase fraction. The direction of the proposed mediator's effect is therefore internally inconsistent.
